headline: Fear holds as hawkish Fed bets meet rising oil-driven jitters
body: Markets are closed through the long weekend — quiet Sunday trading ahead of Monday's holiday — so sentiment is still working off Friday's session, which closed lower across the board: the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,718.60, the Nasdaq slipped 0.3% to 26,506.99, and the Dow dropped 271.86 points (0.5%) to 53,414.25. The trigger was August's jobs report, with nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against estimates near 53,000-55,000 and unemployment holding at 4.1% — a beat strong enough that traders read it as ammunition for the Fed's hawks rather than reassurance about the economy. Odds of a hike at the September 16 meeting have climbed into the high-50s to mid-60s percent range, up sharply from roughly a coin flip a week earlier, and the 2-year Treasury yield pushed to its highest level since January 2025.

Layered on top of the rate repricing is a fresh geopolitical risk premium: renewed U.S. strikes on Iranian military targets and Iranian retaliation against Gulf allies, including missile fire toward Kuwait, have pushed Brent crude above $97 and WTI near $92, with oil up roughly 9% on the week. The combination has the CNN Fear & Greed Index sitting in the low-40s — fear territory, little changed from the prior session. Retail chatter leans single-stock rather than macro: StockTwits activity clusters around Nike (fresh multi-year lows and a looming index removal), Roblox (selling off after pulling full-year guidance), BioNTech (an FDA fast-track designation) and speculative interest in Eastman Kodak's manufacturing pivot. There's no sign of a coordinated retail wave in either direction, so today's read leans more on the jobs-and-Fed storyline and the oil-driven geopolitical overhang than on any clear social-sentiment signal.
